sources: Penn State Extension, House Centipedes (S. Jacobs): females can survive several years and produce up to 150 young; body 1-1.5 in, 3-4 in with legs and antennae; native to the Mediterranean, first recorded in Pennsylvania in 1849; hide in floor drains without water traps, cement block walls, under cardboard boxes, crawl spaces; can't survive PA winters outdoors but reproduce in heated buildings; eat silverfish, firebrats, carpet beetle larvae, cockroaches, spiders; larvae hatch with 4 pairs of legs, 13 pairs before adolescence; https://extension.psu.edu/house-centipedes

title: 150 Babies in Your Bathroom 🐛 (Things Living In Your House #37)
tiktok_caption: house centipede in your bathroom? 🐛 one female can make up to 150 babies, and if you grab a leg it snaps off and she keeps running. Let it stay or get it out? 🐛 stay / 🚪 out #housecentipede #bugsinyourhouse #centipede #meatballmyths

beats.say: One centipede in your bathroom can make up to 150 babies.
Grab its leg, and the leg snaps off. It keeps running.
It breaks at a weak spot built into the leg, on purpose.
And the leg can grow back over its next molts.
Lose it young, and the new leg grows back slower.
It crawls up through floor drains with no water trap.
By day it hides inside cement block walls.
Or under the cardboard boxes stacked on your basement floor.
Legs and feelers, it's up to four inches across.
The body itself? Only about an inch long.
It comes from around the Mediterranean Sea.
It was first found in Pennsylvania in 1849.
In summer, it can hunt outside, right along your walls.
Up north, it can't survive the winter outside.
So it breeds where it's warm. Inside your heated house.
It eats firebrats, silverfish, roaches and spiders.
A baby hatches with just a few legs and adds more each molt.
Six baby stages, then four more, before it's grown up.
Can it bite you? If you grab it, it might.
Bug experts say it's rare, and not dangerous.
It would much rather run away from you.
Want fewer? Fix the damp spots, and seal the dry drains.
